finding.title: Too many doors: 22 menu items, 7 second-level menus, ~110 screens
finding.evidence: An owner with every module sees 22 sidebar items in 4 groups; 9 of them open the same /dashboard page in a side panel. Advertising, Inventory, Customer Messaging, WhatsApp, Automations, Staff and Settings each add their own second menu, and Email adds a third level (sidebar → Settings menu → email tabs). finding.customer-impact: A merchant can't form a picture of "where things are"; every visit starts with hunting.

finding.title: Messaging is split into four separate products
finding.evidence: SMS = "Customer Messaging" (13 pages). WhatsApp = 8 tabs under /dashboard/whatsapp-automation. Email = 7 tabs inside Settings. Plus an "Automations" hub that covers SMS and email but not WhatsApp. Result: 6 places to build an automation (SMS builder, SMS "Advanced settings", SMS Setup step 5, WhatsApp builder, Email 7-step builder, hub 4-step wizard), 3 template editors with 3 variable syntaxes ({{customer_name}}, {{customer_first_name}}, {{customer.first_name}}), 4 message histories, 3 consent / do-not-contact lists, 3 change logs, test phones added in 5 places, business name / quiet hours / daily caps / pause-all set separately per channel.
finding.customer-impact: The merchant has to learn the same idea three or four times with different words and rules.

finding.title: Nothing works until the merchant finishes long setups; nothing is on by default
finding.evidence: Before the first customer message: SMS ≈ 5 setup steps + AWS sender approval + phone code + budget + consent basis + master switch + leaving sandbox, then a 5-step automation. WhatsApp ≈ choose connection type and accept risks, scan, configure, verify number, test, write a template on another tab, 5-step automation, untick "Test mode". Email ≈ connect a mailbox (or SMTP + sender code), write an HTML template, activate it, 7-step automation. product.onboarding: Wati: one path via Meta Embedded Signup (choose option → business details → "Continue with Facebook" → number and display name → Finish), or "Coexistence" (keep the WhatsApp Business app; scan a QR; sync up to 180 days of chats). Interakt: 3 steps with a trial while Meta verification is pending. product.patterns: Triple Whale: one summary dashboard with a section per source, tiles you can pin/hide (snippet). Polar: anomaly alerts by email/Slack; AI daily digest (vendor). Lifetimely: setup checklist 0/5 in the corner, default gross margin when costs are unknown, an AI agent that says what changed, why, and the next move — merchant approves. product.patterns: Inventory Planner's landing page: stock value, items to replenish, overstock, best sellers; each recommendation says what to buy, how much, and "potential lost revenue", with "how this was calculated". shared-patterns.pattern: Home = a few numbers + "what needs you" (Shopify, Klaviyo, Inventory Planner).
Alerts appear only when something is wrong, at the top (Klaviyo, Peel, Polar).
Every change explained as: what changed, why, what to do (Lifetimely, Sidekick, Peel).
The product recommends; the merchant approves (Sidekick, Lifetimely).
The essential automations are created and switched on during setup (Klaviyo, Shopify Messaging).
Templates arrive fully filled in — trigger, timing, wording (Omnisend, Klaviyo, AiSensy).
Branding and sender are taken from the store automatically (Klaviyo, Shopify, Omnisend).
Setup is short, skippable, resumable, with visible progress (Lifetimely 0/5, Klaviyo, Deputy).
Defaults stand in for inputs the merchant doesn't have (Lifetimely default margin, TrueProfit auto costs).
Compliance handled by the product, shown as a fact, not a form (Postscript quiet hours, Shopify STOP line).
All channels in one messaging area; channel is a choice per message (Shopify Messaging, Omnisend, Klaviyo).
One Connections page in Settings with simple status words (Klaviyo, Polar, Omnisend).
Numbers reach the merchant outside the app: daily digest, push alerts (Peel, Polar, Triple Whale, TrueProfit).
Mobile shows a handful of pinned numbers (TrueProfit, Shopify).
People help with the hard parts — included onboarding (Polar, Prediko, Interakt).

automation-by-default.rule: When Shopify connects, create the recommended automations as drafts with brand, sender and wording filled in from the store.
Email: switch the transactional ones on as soon as a mailbox is connected (with a clear "On — turn off" toggle and a duplicate-notification warning if Shopify's own emails are on).

WhatsApp and SMS: switch on after the channel connects and the merchant picks a consent basis once; submit the needed WhatsApp templates to Meta automatically and show "Waiting for Meta approval (usually under 24 h)".
Test mode turns itself off after the first successful test; no separate "Practice run / Dry run / Test mode" words.

Defaults for everything a merchant can't decide on day one: SMS budget (e.g. US$20/month, adjustable), quiet hours 9 pm–8 am in the customer's time zone, one message per customer per day, overtime and break policies by country.

whatsapp-simplification.step: One "Connect WhatsApp" button. Default to Meta's Embedded Signup in "keep using my WhatsApp Business app" (Coexistence) mode once Meta approves bizinsights as a Tech Provider; until then the QR link, explained in one sentence ("Works like WhatsApp Web; keep your phone online"), with the risks behind "Learn more".
Hide the token form and Cloud API vocabulary behind "Advanced".

Verify the merchant's own number automatically (already done for the linked number) and send the test with one button.
